title: Audit record duplication and TTL mismatch after KMS epoch switchover
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: During the KMS epoch switchover on 2026-02-18 we observed a class of audit log anomalies: duplicated audit entries for a subset of SSO-authenticated requests and TTL values written to the audit store that did not match the active retention policy. Scope: ~0.6% of audit events across auth-proxy and token-broker flows for a 45-minute window. Root cause hypothesis: race between KMS epoch handler and audit-writer backfill job that retried on transient key lookup errors, causing duplicated writes with stale TTL metadata.

Impact: compliance-sensitive customers saw duplicate events in their audit exports and retention tooling flagged inconsistent TTL values, causing two customers to request manual reconciliation. No plaintext secrets leaked and auth checks remained correct; primary impact is audit integrity and downstream compliance automation.

Goal: remediate residual inconsistent records, harden write path to prevent duplication on transient KMS errors, add end-to-end detection for TTL mismatches, and formalize runbook for future KMS switchover operations.

Acceptance criteria:
- All inconsistent audit records identified and reconciled or flagged; reconciliation script committed and run with verification report in S3.
- Audit-writer ensures idempotent writes for retried events (dedupe by event fingerprint + epoch) and writes canonical TTL based on retention policy.
- Add unit and integration tests covering KMS transient failures + writer retries.
- Runbook updated and reviewed; +1 from Security and Compliance.
action_items: Run dedupe/reconcile script across affected audit partitions and upload reconciliation report to s3://redwood-incident-reports/ENG-62887/reconcile-2026-03-04.csv
Implement idempotency key in audit-writer (fingerprint = sha256(user|ts|request_id|kms_epoch)) and enforce upsert semantics
Ensure TTL is computed at writer time using canonical retention lookup and not copied from retried payloads
Add integration test that simulates KMS lookup failures and verifies single write with correct TTL
Update KMS switchover playbook with pre-switchover audit-writer quiesce step and post-switchover validation queries
Coordinate a compliance-facing summary and remediation timeline with Customer Success for affected customers
